note: Three 7th chords on one root, each shown with only its root and the notes that make it different lit, one view per chord, then named by ear in the chord game. Each step is a tap on the neck, not a description of the sound.

exercise.title: Three 7th chords on C
exercise.focus: Cmaj7 · C7 · Cm7 · naming 7th chords by ear
exercise.why: Each of these 7th chords differs from the next by one note, so compare them side by side.

sections.text: Cmaj7 has {{7}} (B), a half step under the root. Tap {{1}} then {{7}} on the neck. Then tap through the whole chord.
C7 has {{b7}} (B♭) instead, a whole step under the root. Tap {{1}} then {{b7}}. Then tap through the chord. Go back to Cmaj7 above to compare.
Cm7 keeps {{b7}}. Its 3rd drops a half step to {{b3}} (E♭). Tap {{1}} {{b3}} {{b7}}, then the whole chord.
The game plays a chord on a random root. Pick its name: major, minor, dominant 7, major 7 or minor 7. Listen to the top note first: a half step under the octave means maj7.
